name: Indiana
basePeriod: The first four of the last five completed calendar quarters before your claim. Indiana has no general alternate base period.
notModeled: Enter the quarters in order, earliest first: the $2,500 test is on the last two.

citation.sourceNote: IC 22-4-12-2: the weekly amount is "forty-seven percent (47%) of the claimant's prior average weekly wage", rounded down, the average being base-period wage credits "divided by ... fifty-two (52)", and it "may not exceed three hundred ninety dollars ($390)." DWD's handbook works it: "$30,000 ÷ 52 = $576.92 x 0.47 = $271". IC 22-4-14-5: at least $2,500 in the last two quarters, $4,200 in all four, and 1.5 times the high quarter. IC 22-4-12-4: the total "shall not exceed twenty-six (26) times the individual's weekly benefit, or twenty-eight percent (28%) of the individual's wage credits", rounded down. Indiana pays no dependent allowance. One unpaid waiting week. Read 2026-10-19.
